_comment_key_facts: key_facts = the load-bearing factual claims a position rests on, each paired with the EXTERNAL source it came from. Added 2026-08-11 after a prior revision inverted the direction of a source's anchor move and then survived TWO re-verifications, because each re-verification re-read my own note and reproduced the error. A re-verification that does not diff the recorded claim against the source's actual words is confirmation, not verification. The audit rotation surfaces these for source-diffing. TAGGING CAVEAT (2026-08-12): the audit tags a source UNVERIFIED when it does not start with http, but a URL that 403s (congress.gov) is no more agent-verifiable than a prose 'sweep'. Where that happens, say so INLINE in the claim and name the independent falsifier used instead — do not let an unfetchable URL launder a claim into looking checked. SOURCE_DATE (2026-08-12): distinct from `checked`. `checked` is when I last LOOKED; `source_date` is when the source was PUBLISHED. The MacBook staleness cost 18pp precisely because those diverged invisibly — checked=1d ago on a source published 114d earlier, in a story that had moved three times since. For live-state sources (a leaderboard, an order book, a market description) the two are equal by construction. ATOMICITY REQUIRED (2026-08-13): one independently checkable assertion per entry, each with its own source and source_date. Bundled entries are how an unchecked fact hides inside a checked one — SpaceX's 'No plausible 2026 rival: OpenAI pushed to 2027, and a >$2.1T close would need an S-1 already public' bundled OpenAI's TIMING (checked twice) with every other rival's SIZE (never checked), and the second cost the project its largest prior correction. If an entry contains ' and ' joining two verifiable claims, split it. SOURCE TAXONOMY (2026-08-13) — 'is it a URL' is the WRONG test and my first sweep miscategorised because of it. Ranked by what may move a number: (1) FIRST-HAND MEASUREMENT — a CLOB book walk, a gamma/API read, an on-chain balance. Reproducible on demand and STRONGER than any article, even though it carries no URL. (2) DATED PRIMARY ARTIFACT — a fetched, dated piece; the standard for a factual claim about the world. (3) NAMED BUT UNLINKED — e.g. 'third-party trackers'; verifiable with effort, acceptable if the claim is checked periodically. (4) AGGREGATED SEARCH SUMMARY — a LEAD ONLY. It must never move a prior: on 2026-08-13 one such summary said the M5 reshuffle was an 'acceleration', moved MacBook 0.62->0.58, and pinning it to dated sources REFUTED it outright. Label the kind when the source is not a URL, so a future sweep does not mistake a measurement for a guess.

At 14:12 UTC the refreshed normalized market distribution assigned 0.4557 to the held 295-339 union; all buckets remained active, unclosed and without UMA status. A complete 20/20/20 exit was $8.45 fee-free.

Circulating 53.5%-54% United Russia exit-poll claims disclose no named pollster, sample or method. VCIOM explicitly warned on September 17 that it publishes no interim exit-poll results and that figures attributed to it before polls close are unreliable; the rumors therefore receive no independent evidentiary weight beyond the observed market move.

FOM's September 10 preliminary forecast, based on September 4-6 fieldwork, puts United Russia at 47-49%, CPRF at 14-17%, LDPR at 10-12%, New People at 8-9%, and Just Russia at 6-7%. Normalizing the five qualifying-party midpoints implies about 121 of 225 list seats for United Russia; adding APEK's 185-195 district range centers near 311 total seats.

Andrei Pertsev's September 16 Carnegie analysis expects more than 200 United Russia district winners. Its underlying August 4 RBC investigation confirms 16 negotiated opposition concessions but also identifies up to 15 additional competitive districts, making roughly 200-205 a meaningful high-district scenario rather than an observed result. Combined with the list forecasts, this shifts probability toward 325-339 and above 339 without increasing the 295-339 union prior.

Turovsky's September 11 commentary argues APEK may understate United Russia's district wins: LDPR and New People are unlikely to win the forecast districts without explicit United Russia concessions, of which he identifies few. He gives no numerical replacement forecast or confidence interval.

VCIOM's September 10 turnout-adjusted forecast puts United Russia at 51-53%, CPRF at 13-15%, New People and LDPR at 9-11% each, and Just Russia at 4-6%. It supplies no district forecast; normalized list seats combined with APEK's district range center near 319 total seats if Just Russia passes and 326 if it misses.
APEK's September 10 express forecast puts United Russia's party-list vote at 49-52%.
APEK's September 10 express forecast puts United Russia's single-member-district wins at 185-195.

Criteria re-read without drift: this bucket resolves on United Russia's State Duma seats resulting from the election, first by consensus credible reporting and, if ambiguous, solely by official Russian-government results; if results remain indefinite after May 31, 2027, the lowest bracket wins.
APEK's August 10 forecast puts United Russia's party-list vote at 51-54%.
APEK's August 10 forecast puts United Russia's single-member-district wins at 190-197.

An independent RASO survey of 54 political-technology experts forecasts United Russia at 95-130 party-list seats and 155-210 district seats. The very broad component ranges center near 295 total, shifting probability below the prior APEK-centered distribution and failing to confirm the union add gate.

VCIOM's weekly series now ends September 6: United Russia support is 37.4%, versus 37.2% on August 30. This near-flat raw voting-intention measure does not replace VCIOM's turnout-adjusted election forecast or APEK's district forecast, so it does not justify moving the three-bucket distribution.

PolitPro's as-of-September-4 page displays 234 ER seats from its national Election Trend. The number is mechanically 47.0 / 90.4 qualifying-party vote x 450 = 234, proving the generic display proportionally allocates the whole chamber and does not model Russia's 225 single-member districts. Its newest conventional poll inputs are still August 23. Treat it only as a qualitative downside sensitivity, not an independent whole-seat forecast.

September 13 final-campaign commentary says divergent forecasts reflect a material undecided bloc and regional variation in United Russia's result; it supplies no new numerical national vote or district-seat forecast. A separate same-day commentary still expects KPRF to finish second. This widens uncertainty but does not displace the Sep-10 FOM/VCIOM/APEK inputs.

VCIOM's September 14 campaign-awareness survey, fielded September 9-12, reports that 76% of respondents expect United Russia to win. It provides campaign visibility and expected-winner data but no party-list vote forecast, district-seat forecast, or whole-seat distribution, so it confirms favorite status without moving the 295-339 bucket probabilities.

Pravdaserm's September 16 final party-list forecast puts United Russia at 38.6%, but its method multiplies reputation by search-query volume and party-specific turnout coefficients reverse-fitted from 2021; its September 9 raw information-share series assigned New People 76.8%. It has no district-seat forecast. Treat this as a low-quality downside sensitivity that does not displace the Sep-10 FOM/VCIOM/APEK evidence or move the held complete-set distribution.
At September 20 18:04 UTC, the official CEC Telegram feed still contained no party-seat total; its published schedule placed preliminary-results reporting in the 18:00-19:00 UTC window.

At September 20 18:04 UTC all seven exact Gamma buckets remained active, unclosed and UMA-clear. Normalized midpoints assigned 0.291 to 295-339; a synchronized protected-group walk realized only $4.52 for 20/20/20, a 0.226 payout-unit breakeven.

At 18:00 UTC, VCIOM's official exit poll reported United Russia 49.4%, KPRF 14.2%, LDPR 10.7%, New People 9.7% and Just Russia 6.6%; INSOMAR reported 52.8%, 14.8%, 9.9%, 8.6% and 5.5%. These are party-list votes, not district or total-seat results. Early CEC reporting likewise gave only a 57.54% United Russia list share.

RBC's article published at September 20 22:00:27 UTC reported 45.08% of protocols counted: United Russia 57.67%, KPRF 13.81%, LDPR 8.88%, New People 7.87% and Just Russia 5.18%. It explicitly estimated 138-139 United Russia list seats, reported United Russia leading 200 single-member districts, and reported 16 other leads with nine districts lacking preliminary data.

At September 20 22:14 UTC, Gamma remained active, unclosed and UMA-clear. The 295-309 YES book had no bid; 20 shares of 310-324 and 325-339 could sell for $0.12 and $1.80 respectively, not a synchronized complete-set exit.

At September 21 01:52 UTC, CEC-linked reporting showed United Russia leading 208 of 225 single-member districts, with only two districts still at 0% protocols. At 01:48 UTC, 75.31% of list protocols put United Russia at 57.48%; normalizing over the five parties above 5% implies about 139 list seats and a provisional total near 347 before the last two districts.

At the September 21 02:04 UTC execution check, 295-309 had no YES bid, 310-324 bid 0.003, and 325-339 bid 0.011. All markets remained active, unclosed, unresolved and UMA-clear. DEC-0166 sold all 20 of the effectively impossible 310-324 YES leg FOK at 0.003 for 0.06 pUSD; the matched order and pUSD balance reconciled.

At September 21 05:11 UTC, TASS/CEC reported 90.43% of protocols with United Russia at 57.86% and Just Russia at 4.95%, below the 5% threshold. RBC subsequently reported United Russia leading 209 of 225 districts. DEC-0167 sold all 20 of the 325-339 YES leg FOK at 0.011 for 0.22 pUSD after p_yes fell to about 0.006.

At September 21 10:08 UTC, TASS reported United Russia leading 208 of 225 districts after 95.97% of district protocols and only four parties above 5% after 95.45% of list protocols. RBC's 95.18% snapshot projected 355 United Russia seats with Just Russia at 4.96%, while CEC chair Ella Pamfilova said Just Russia retained a large chance to cross 5%. Either allocation branch remains far above 309. The exact 295-309 market was active and UMA-null but still had no YES bid.
